newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADA EXPANDS ECONOMIC SANCTIONS AGAINST BURMA.
newsitem.headline: CANADA EXPANDS ECONOMIC SANCTIONS AGAINST BURMA.

text.p: Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy on Thursday announced further economic sanctions against Burma to increase pressure on the country's military leaders to improve human rights and move toward democracy.

Canada is withdrawing Burma's General Preferential Tariff eligibilty and requiring all domestic exporters to Burma to have an export permit, according to a statement released by the Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade.

"Burma's military leaders have made no effort to improve the current situation and have repeatedly failed to respond to the international community's attempts to open channels of communication,' Axworthy said.

"The actions we have taken today are intended to convey the seriousness of our concerns over the suppression of political freedoms and our frustration with Burma's failure to curb the production and trafficking of illegal drugs," Axworthy said.
Canada said Burma is also the largest source for illegal heroin entering North America.

The government statement said the measures "underscore Canada's concern over the deteriorating human rights situation in Burma and are intended to encourage the military regime to enter into meaningful political dialogue with the leaders of the democracy movement."
Axworthy also announced C$350 million (US$252.3 million) in humanitarian aid for Burmese refugees in Thailand.

Canada suspsended bilateral aid to Burma in 1988 and had previously cut off military sales, supspended its diplomatic presence and frozen export aid and commercial promotion for Canadian firms doing business in Burma.
Canada maintains a dialogue with Burmese human rights activist Aung San Suu Kyi through Canada's ambassador to Burma, who is resident in Thailand.
